Problem 3 (thin evidence), the stance and the codes, written before reading Gioia et al. 2013, Grodal et al. 2021 or any room. STANCE. (1) Two kinds of thin: rare-thin, where few rooms can carry the claim because the event is rare by its nature (a loss then a move; a broken deal); weak-thin, where many rooms carry both elements but the order barely beats its null. (2) A count decides a claim about a distribution or an order across rooms when its denominator is large enough for the null to separate; a weak-thin order is stated as a tendency near its null, whatever I believe. The words may still show the mechanism in the rooms that run it; that is a separate claim, of the words kind, read with codes written first. (3) My reading decides, with the count beside it, a rare-thin claim when the event is rare by its nature, the step shows in members' words in the rooms that carry it, and no room shows the reverse; it then stands as a mechanism shown in N rooms, labelled thin (rule 8), not as a tendency (rule 16). (4) Composition: a rare-thin arrow at the population level may be strong inside a branch; name its rooms for the return. READS (every room carrying both, first concept of each element, read whole, c2_first_concepts.py on c2_elements_c5c2.json). A10, K02 to P10, 21 rooms, codes: J, a judgment of too few hands or too little space comes before the move, and the move follows a loss or erosion of the spot; M, the move comes first and any judgment after it; C, the move is by choice or a coalition's plan, not after a loss; N, the P10 concept is not a move by the room. Note whether the judgment speaks for the room or for one member apart. Rule: if J is at least half of J+M+C, A10 stands as a mechanism shown in N rooms, labelled thin, its bound naming the M and C rooms; if J is under a third, A10 is bounded to its J rooms; if J is 2 or fewer, it is dropped. Rule 6 check: rooms carrying K02 but no P10, and of these how many the record says lost their work (work_remained). A05, P08 to P07, 158 rooms, codes: L, the sparing concept names a border, truce, deal, policy or agreement (the line); T, sparing with none named (tacit); O, not sparing a neighbour. A14, P08 to P16, 214 rooms, codes: C, the help concept names a deal, border, truce or the neighbour relation as its ground or route (the channel); H, help with none named; O, not help between rooms. Rule for A05 and A14: L (or C) of L+T (or C+H), reported where the order holds and where it fails; if at least half where the order holds, the mechanism shows in words and the arrow stands thin by its order; if under a third, the mechanism is marked theorised and the arrow stands as an order near its null. The stance checked against the method's sources, cited from the page (sources-from-J). Gioia, Corley and Hamilton 2013: the study of social construction focuses 'less on the number or frequency of measureable occurrences' (p. 16); qualitative work is suspected of theorizing 'on the basis of rather thin evidence', and the answer is to show the evidence ('Where is the evidence for your assertions?', p. 18), which the data structure does; attention goes to nascent concepts without adequate referents (p. 20). Grodal, Anteby and Holm 2021: 'Not all information is equally important in the categorization process' (p. 597); negative cases and unusual incidents matter in theorizing 'even if there is only one case' (p. 598, quoting Emerson, Fretz and Shaw 2011); a category 'abundant in the data' was dropped as peripheral to the theory (p. 599); propositions are held loosely, each conjecture rated 'strong, qualified, neutral, or contradictory' as a safeguard against premature closure (p. 604, quoting Miles et al. 2014). The stance stands: frequency does not set importance, but a thin claim must show its evidence and carry its rating. One addition: the four ratings map onto the model's labels (strong, fair, thin) and add 'contradictory', which the A10 rule already has (the reverse).
